hypothesis: If the generated ERA5 pressure-level Zarr pipeline preserves lossless Blosc-Zstd clevel=9 bitshuffle, exact selected values, and chunks equivalent to one time, one pressure-level plane, and full latitude/longitude, but groups channels from the same source variable into a single native variable array with a real selected pressure-level dimension, then output_bytes may decrease by eliminating duplicate data-array metadata and per-channel selector-coordinate arrays while keeping each requested field-selector plane independently addressable through dataset_artifact channel selectors.
reflection: The parent is feasible and already uses the best measured compression family so far for footprint: lossless Blosc-Zstd bitshuffle at clevel 9, with output_bytes 104,831,028 and exact semantic equivalence. Chunk payload dominates, but clevel is already at the Blosc maximum, so a safe next footprint mutation should not weaken compression or try lossy packing. The remaining bounded opportunity is to reduce duplicated Zarr arrays and selector-coordinate metadata while preserving sample/selector/full-spatial chunking: publish one native data array per source variable containing exactly the requested pressure levels for that variable, rather than one data array per field-selector channel. Prior feasible evidence shows this kind of source-variable grouping can satisfy the artifact/consumer interface when selector chunk size remains 1. Expected byte gains are modest because metadata is small, but this is aligned with the scheduled output_bytes objective and does not drop any field or plane.
